z-m-24-01.title: One solution line erase a root
z-m-24-01.topic: Roots lost when dividing both equation sides by same expression
z-m-24-01.goal: Find line where root disappear, generalise equation conditions causing this, make your own examples and explain.
z-m-24-01.material: Jia solve x³=4x and write roots 2 and −2 only. Doyun say different from his answer but give no reason. All x real here. Read x³ cubed, x² squared.
z-m-24-01.thinking.1: Judge conditions where expression transformation changes solution set
z-m-24-01.prereq.0: H2 marks difficulty/support only, not school grade. Assume learned factoring quadratic equations in middle school and cubic factoring in Common Math.
z-m-24-01.prereq.1: Plug value into equation and check if both sides equal
z-m-24-01.s.s1.prompt: Dis Jia solution. Choose line making it wrong or where mistake show.
z-m-24-01.s.s1.hint.0: Check line by line whether equation has same roots as previous line.
z-m-24-01.s.s1.hint.1: Put x=0,2,−2 into original x³=4x one by one and check. [0 2]
z-m-24-01.s.s1.line.1: Divide both sides by x: x²=4.
z-m-24-01.s.s1.line.4: So equation roots na 2 and −2, two roots.
z-m-24-01.s.s1.explain: Line 2 divide by x, but x=0 makes both sides original 0, so e also solution. They no check x=0 separately, root 0 lost, leading to “two.” Lines 3–4 correctly solve after division. Original real roots are −2,0,2. [2 0 0 0 0 5 3 4 2 0 2]
z-m-24-01.s.s2.prompt: All equations below solved over reals. Which one loses no original roots if you divide both sides by shown expression and solve remaining equation?
z-m-24-01.s.s2.hint.0: For each equation, check if some x make divisor zero. [0]
z-m-24-01.s.s2.hint.1: Substitute those x into original equation both sides; also check if any equation has no real x making divisor zero.
z-m-24-01.s.s2.r.a: You no check both sides at value making x−2=0 in original equation.
z-m-24-01.s.s2.r.b: You miss divisor-zero value fit also solve original. Put x=0 in. [0 0]
z-m-24-01.s.s2.r.c: Dis choice use criterion whether real x can make divisor zero. [0]
z-m-24-01.s.s2.r.d: Even with square, when x−1=0 both sides 0. Check if that value solution.
z-m-24-01.s.s2.explain: If both sides f·g=f·h, any f=0 value always solution. If real x make f zero, handle separately before dividing. x²+3≥3 for every real, never zero, so option c no lose root x=4 by division. Over complex numbers, x²+3=0 roots also matter, so different. [0 0 3 3 0 4 3 0]
z-m-24-01.s.s3.prompt: Make 3 equations (x−a)(x−b)=c(x−a), a,b,c integers −9..9, c≠0. Dividing by x−a must lose one negative root a, while remaining root b+c positive. [3 9 9 0]
z-m-24-01.s.s3.hint.0: Choose negative a first, then adjust b,c so b+c positive.
z-m-24-01.s.s3.hint.1: Substitute x=a into both sides of your equation and check.
z-m-24-01.s.s3.explain: For example a=−3,b=1,c=2: (x+3)(x−1)=2(x+3). Divide by x+3 gives x=3 only, but x=−3 make both sides 0, so solution too. Move everything left: (x+3)(x−3)=0, roots −3,3. Count equations same if roots a and b+c equal; if differ, different. [3 3]
z-m-24-01.s.s3.because.prompt: Choose one equation you made; write numerical root lost by dividing x−a and explain.
z-m-24-01.s.s3.because.hint.0: Calculate both sides after substituting x=a.
z-m-24-01.s.s3.because.hint.1: Compare root from division with root from moving all terms to one side.
z-m-24-01.s.s3.because.selfAssess.0: Did your numbers confirm lost root make both original sides equal?

z-m-24-01.s.s3.because.selfAssess.2: Did you think of a way to find all roots without division, e.g. move everything and factor?

z-m-24-01.s.s3.because.model.1: For (x+1)(x−4)=−1(x+1), divide by x+1 to get x−4=−1, x=3. But x=−1 makes x+1 zero and both sides equal, so also root; division by zero lose am. [1 4 1 1 1 4 1 3 1 1 0 1 0]
z-m-24-01.s.s3.because.modelNote.1: You first state root from division, then lost root too.

z-m-24-02.title: How many solutions for problem with no range?
z-m-24-02.topic: Number of roots of x³=1 and number ranges
z-m-24-02.goal: Work out range solution belongs to; keep/revise root-count judgment as info arrive; confirm with range-dependent answer and roots you find.
z-m-24-02.material: Find roots x³=1, but x range missing. Minsu compare sizes, Seoyun ask “should choose range first?” Info show one piece at a time, judge each time. x³ read x cubed.
z-m-24-02.thinking.1: Revise or keep judgment with new info
z-m-24-02.thinking.3: Find and verify several roots yourself
z-m-24-02.prereq.0: H2 marks difficulty/support only, not school grade. Assume Common Math complex number meaning (i²=−1), multiplication, discriminant, cubic factoring learned.
z-m-24-02.prereq.1: Two complex numbers equal iff real parts equal and imaginary parts equal.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.prompt: Info reveal one at a time. Choose judgment each time and see if new info change or keep it.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.hint.0: When new info appear, reread earlier choice and write briefly what change.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.hint.1: Before choosing, check “which number range” option assume.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.0.info: Equation x³=1, x range absent. Minsu: “x=1 solution. If x>1 then x³>1; if x<1 then x³<1; so only solution 1.” Read > greater than, < less than.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.0.after: If x real, Minsu argument correct. But range no state, so no know if real numbers enough. [1 1 1]
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.0.o.a: All numbers fit compare by size, so only solution 1.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You no consider all numbers can line up by greater/less. Which number types fit compare size?
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Correct for real x, but range missing, so need more checking.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You notice which numbers solution assume and include missing range in judgment.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Cubic equation must get three roots, so one-root answer wrong.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You infer count from degree only. Number distinct roots depends expression and range.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.0.o.d: You only substitute x=1, so solution tells nothing.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Solution also considers x>1 and x<1. Read what that proves.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.1.info: Two new info: (1) x³−1=(x−1)(x²+x+1); quadratic discriminant 1−4=−3. (2) Book intro says unit solves equations in complex numbers, but problem itself no range. [1 1 1 1 1 0 1 4 3 2]
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.1.ask: Now how answer “how many distinct roots”?
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.1.after: x−1=0 gives real root 1. x²+x+1=0 negative discriminant, so no real roots but two different imaginary roots. Real range: 1; complex range: 3. Since range unclear, either give range-dependent answer or assume unit means complex and answer 3. Minsu real-number claim stays correct.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.1.o.a: No range stated, so only consider reals and answer 1.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Correct within real range, but you ignore new discriminant and unit info.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Discriminant −3 negative, so no solution in any number range.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Discriminant concerns factor x²+x+1. You forget other factor x−1.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You include unresolved range condition in answer; result depend on conditions.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Follow unit note, assume complex and answer 3 while stating assumption.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.1.r.d: You use unit clue and state assumption, giving both evidence and limit.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.2.info: Let imaginary root ω=(−1+√3i)/2. i²=−1. ω root of x²+x+1=0. Check directly if ω also satisfy x³=1. [1 3 2 1 1 3 2 1 0 1]
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.2.ask: Which checking methods valid? Several fit.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.2.after: Both exact methods: a use ω²+ω+1=0; c calculate ω² then multiply. Approximate b only catch arithmetic mistake, no proof; d assume conclusion. This imaginary root also satisfy x³=1, supporting 3 complex roots.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You choose reduce ω³ to linear in ω using known identity.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Write ω=−0.5+0.87i, multiply repeatedly; if near 1, consider checked.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Approximate values help check, but no prove exactly 1.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Find ω² then multiply by ω: (−1+√3i)(−1−√3i)/4=1.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You choose direct multiplication. Key na how imaginary part disappear.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Since ω root of some equation, assume ω³=1 and use directly.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You assume conclusion you need prove. ω root of x²+x+1=0, not x³=1.
z-m-24-02.s.s1.reflect: If first think only solution 1, what info make that “correct over reals”? Why size comparison no work for imaginary numbers?
z-m-24-02.s.s2.prompt: Suppose z=a+bi, a,b real, and z³=1. Then (a+bi)³=(a³−3ab²)+(3a²b−b³)i, so real part must 1 and imaginary part 0. Enter 3 different roots as (a,b). Round irrational values to 2 decimals; error up to 0.02 allowed. [1 3 3 3 1 3 0 3 0.02]
z-m-24-02.s.s2.hint.0: Check x³−1 at z=1 and find roots of remaining x²+x+1.
z-m-24-02.s.s2.hint.1: Put real part of root in a and coefficient before i in b; calculate if expressions close to 1 and 0.
z-m-24-02.s.s2.explain: Three roots: z=1, z=(−1+√3i)/2, z=(−1−√3i)/2. Decimal pairs about (1,0),(−0.5,0.87),(−0.5,−0.87). Same root with different decimal rounding no count as another. Only root with zero imaginary part na 1; size comparison alone no find other two. [1 1 3 2 1 3 2 1 0 0.5 0.87 0.5 0.87 0 1]
z-m-24-02.s.s2.because.prompt: Explain why Minsu “if x>1 then x³>1, if x<1 then x³<1” no find imaginary roots, and count roots over real and complex ranges. [1 1 1]

z-m-24-02.s.s2.because.hint.1: Split real/complex ranges and count roots found earlier.
z-m-24-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: Did you explain Minsu argument rely on “which numbers can be compared by size”?

z-m-24-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.2: Did you connect imaginary roots with values found (real part −0.5 etc)?
z-m-24-02.s.s2.because.model.0: Minsu correct only for real x. Only real numbers compare by size; imaginary no order, so method cannot find imaginary roots. Real range get 1 root; complex range get 3.
z-m-24-02.s.s2.because.model.1: For complex numbers Minsu method no apply. Imaginary numbers no greater/less relation. Real range one root (1); complex three: 1 and two imaginary roots.
